analysis_notes.gap_analysis: The Torah text (torah_76.txt) contains one occurrence of the word 'בִּבְחִינַת', but it functions as a proof-text citation rather than a true bechina equivalence: the Rebbe says that Israel's act of elevating all fallen places corresponds to the verse 'וְנִשְׁאָר גַּם הוּא לֵאלֹקֵינוּ' (Zechariah 9:8). This is not equating two independent conceptual nodes as parallel expressions of the same essential nature; it is applying a verse to illustrate a process. Similarly, the teaching that גּוֹלָה stands as an acronym (ראשי תיבות) for the verse is a formal linguistic observation, not a bechina pairing. The six concepts present in the text — ישראל בגלות, מקומות שפלים ונפולים (fallen/low places that Israel elevates), בני הגולה (the name Israel bears in exile), גולה (the word whose letters encode the verse), בתי טרטיאות וקרקסאות (theaters and circuses — examples of fallen places destined to become Torah houses), and the verse וְנִשְׁאָר גַּם הוּא לֵאלֹקֵינוּ — are related causally and formally, not via bechina equating.
